newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares creep up to 16-month high.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares creep up to 16-month high.

text.p: Egyptian shares maintained their uptrend on Thursday, creeping 0.01 points up to a new 16-month high on gains in the popular cement and milling sectors.
The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) overall index closed at 235.05 points, its highest since late April 1995, on average volume of 25.52 million pounds ($7.52 million).
"The market is still going up with ever increasing newcomers," said Elwi Taimour of Financial Brokerage Group.
Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries was the market leader jumping 13.00 pounds to close at 145.00, after shares worth 5.38 million pounds were traded.
"This share fell too much during last year's slump and now it's picking up again," said Mohammed Abdullah, vice president brokers at Hermes Financial.
"The market for Eipico been dry for at least 10 days now and so what shares were put up for sale were snapped up," he added.
North Cairo Flour Mills was the second most active stock, with shares worth 4.86 million pounds trading. The share ended unchanged at 100.00 pounds.
"The whole milling sector is going up, after the state sold off more than 50 percent of Central and West Delta Flour Mills," Taimour said.
The government had said it would not privatise more than 40 percent in the sector, regarding it as strategic.
Southern Cairo Flour Mills finished 1.00 pound up to 54.00 pounds. Central Egypt Flour Mills also rose 0.29 pounds to 28.00 pounds.

Suez Cement closed 0.30 pounds up at 46.70 after shares worth 1.45 million pounds changed hands. The firm is still performing well since the National Bank of Egypt said it would sell all or most of the 15 percent it holds in the firm through a GDR.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 350.39 points from 350.95 on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms remained unchanged at 160.74.
